query: In September, how did refined oil product flows from the Gulf region compare with preconflict levels?

results.text: Global oil supply is projected to fall by 5.5 mb/d (5.2 percent) in 2026, the largest decline in more than four decades outside the 2020 global recession. Modest increases in oil output in advanced economies, such as Canada and the United States, as well as in Latin America and the Caribbean, are on track to offset only a small share of very large production losses in the Middle East (figure 4.C). Next year, operational adaptations that have facilitated increased crude oil exports from the Gulf region in recent months are assumed to remain effective, allowing shipments to continue gradually building. A recovery in the global production of refined products is likely to lag. Refinery throughput is anticipated to recover to preconflict levels around mid−2027, as repairs to refineries and export facilities progress in the Middle East and Russia, and refining capacity expands elsewhere.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARYCOMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 1 The state of commodity markets The outlook for commodity markets has become increasingly complex amid potentially reinforcing shocks related to multiple conflict fronts and an unusually powerful El Niño. Crude oil exports from the Gulf region have recently been close to preconflict volumes, aided by pipeline flows and workarounds such as ship-to-ship transfers beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Nonetheless, flows of refined oil products from the region have remained depressed amid damage to refineries, at less than half of preconflict levels in September. Meanwhile attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline and threats to shipping in the Red Sea highlight the potential vulnerability of alternative export routes for crude oil that helped to attenuate disruptions this year.

In 2026Q3, a partial recovery in China’s oil imports, following sharp declines in 2026Q2, eroded a critical source of earlier price relief (figure 7.D). Meanwhile, global observed oil inventories fell: after starting 2026 at about 8,250 million barrels (mb)—close to the top of their 2021-25 range—inventories at end-September were close to the bottom, having fallen more rapidly even than in 2021 (figure 7.E). Key oil product markets tightened sharply due to much Gulf refining capacity offline, and export product restrictions in Russia introduced to safeguard domestic supplies after intensifying Ukrainian attacks. The premium of European diesel over Brent crude reached a record monthly average of about $91/bbl in September, before moderating slightly the following month, while average U.S. retail diesel prices approached $6.2 per gallon for the first time in October (figure 7.F).

query: By how much had the World Bank Group's metals and minerals index risen in 2026 relative to the first nine months of 2025?

results.text: EXECUTIVE SUMMARYCOMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 3 breadbasket region, contributing to a 14 percent increase in global grain prices between June and September. Food prices would likely have risen even more in recent months if not for near-record supplies of staple grains coming out of the global 2025–26 season. The World Bank Group’s metals and minerals index (which excludes precious metals) has increased by 31 percent this year, relative to the first nine months of 2025. Since April, prices of aluminum, copper, and tin have all hit records. Copper mine output has been somewhat lower than anticipated, while aluminum prices were driven to new peaks in May by conflict-related declines in supply from the Middle East. Meanwhile, the prospect of additional U.S. tariffs has increased inventory demand for copper.

Metal prices are forecast to inch down in 2027, but a high-price regime is expected to remain entrenched, with the metals and minerals price index projected to exceed its 2021 peak by 16 percent. Demand for base metals is anticipated to hold firm, underpinned by robust investment in electrification infrastructure, renewable energy, and data centers, which are base-metal-intensive. However, subdued conventional construction in many economies and weakness in China’s steel sector are likely to weigh on iron ore prices. The precious metals price index fell by 7 percent in 2026Q3 after reaching all-time highs earlier in the year. Still, the index is on track to increase by 40 percent in 2026, before drifting lower by 8 percent in 2027 as investor demand moderates.

Metals and minerals The World Bank Group’s metals and minerals price index is projected to reach a new high in 2026, rising by a projected 25 percent (y/y). Prices of base metals, including aluminum, copper, and tin, are on track for large gains reflecting various supply constraints and growing investment in energy transition and other advanced technologies. Meanwhile, iron ore prices weigh on the aggregate index amid tepid traditional construction investment, especially in China.

query: How many people experienced severe food insecurity worldwide in 2025?

results.text: People experiencing severe food insecurity worldwide numbered 779 million in 2025, down from 803 million in 2024 and 837 million in 2021. Even so, efforts to reduce food insecurity have regressed since the 2010s: severe food insecurity affected 9.5 percent of the global population in 2025, compared with an average of 8.1 percent in 2015–19 (figure 6.B). Moreover, the baseline outlook brings an end to the tailwind from falling global food commodity prices between 2023 and 2025, which had put downward pressure on consumer food costs. In this context, EMDE food price inflation picked up to a median of 3.9 percent (y/y) in 2026Q3, from 3.5 percent the previous quarter, and may firm further as sizable increases in grain and oilseed prices feed through.

The number of people experiencing severe food insecurity worldwide fell to about 779 million in 2025 from 803 million in 2024 and 837 million in 2021 (figure 15.B). The 21 percent decline in global food commodity prices between 2022 and 2025 likely contributed to these gains. Even so, severe food insecurity affected 9.5 percent of the global population in 2025, well above the 8.1 percent average in the five years before COVID-19. With food prices forecast to rise by a cumulative 18 percent in 2026–27 amid overlapping weather, logistics, and conflict shocks, this tailwind for the fight against hunger appears set to become a headwind. These challenges are compounded by surging energy prices, which strain household budgets and further erode food affordability.

The number of people experiencing severe food insecurity globally declined slightly in 2025. However, food insecurity remains more prevalent than in the late 2010s, and renewed food price increases anticipated in 2026–27 could reverse recent progress. Sources: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAOSTAT database); Haver Analytics; World Bank.

query: In the energy section, what drove Gulf voyage rates to record highs?

results.text: ENERGY COMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 14 Oil Recent developments In mid-October, front-month Brent futures reached about $110 per barrel (bbl) as markets weighed rising crude supply and an accelerated release of emergency oil stockpiles by International Energy Agency (IEA) members against conflict in the Middle East (figure 7.A). Entering October, average Middle East oil exports approached their 2025 level owing to greater use of ship-to-ship transfers and untracked shipments (figure 7.B). The recovery was concentrated on crude oil and condensates, while oil products exports, including diesel, have lagged, partly because refinery damage. Tanker shortages, which drove Gulf voyage rates to record highs, together with intensifying attacks on vessels, thinning inventories and concerns about longer-term supply, kept Brent prices elevated (figure 7.C).

Natural gas Recent developments Natural gas markets in most regions tightened sharply in 2026Q3 as Middle East tensions re-escalated and the June U.S.–Iran MoU failed to produce a follow-on agreement. Concerns about prolonged Gulf supply disruptions, stronger Asian power-sector demand, and low European inventories drove up European natural gas and Asian LNG prices to more than double their pre-conflict levels by September, with prices continuing to increase in October (figure 10.A). Although LNG shipments via the Strait of Hormuz have started to increase in recent weeks, they remained at about 25 percent of pre-conflict levels in September. Before the recent resurgence, prices had plunged in June after the MoU was signed and backed up LNG cargoes exited the Gulf. In contrast, monthly U.S. natural gas prices were generally below February levels in 2026Q3,
Atlantic Basin refining margins reached record highs.

query: Why is the reported 7.8 billion barrels of observed oil inventories not all immediately usable?

results.text: ENERGY COMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 16 Supply losses have persistently exceeded the reduction in global oil demand since the onset of the Middle East conflict, with the deficit widening sharply in 2026Q2 to 2.9 mb/d but narrowing in the following quarter (figure 8.F). Accordingly, oil inventories have become the fulcrum on which oil markets have balanced. Although global observed oil inventories still total about 7.8 billion barrels, much is in transit or tied up operationally—for instance, to keep pipelines pressurized—and therefore is not readily usable. In this context, OECD member governments’ inventories at end-September were the lowest in more than three decades, with the U.S. strategic reserves the lowest since 1982. Global oil markets have thus become increasingly vulnerable to further supply disruptions.

query: What change in global natural gas production is projected for 2026?

results.text: LNG production is more concentrated in economies heavily affected by the conflict than oil production, and natural gas output in the Middle East is expected to remain below its 2025 level in 2027, in large part because of damage to LNG trains in Qatar. Although natural gas production is projected to expand elsewhere next year, global demand is also anticipated to recover, such that Asian and European markets remain notably tight. Meanwhile, U.S. natural gas prices are forecast to increase by 6 percent in 2027 from much lower levels, partly owing to increasing LNG export demand. Coal prices are on course to climb by 25 percent (y/y) in 2026 on stronger demand and supply constraints. Prices are then projected to ease by 4 percent next year, as demand for coal as a substitute fuel softens amid lower energy prices more broadly and the expansion of renewables.

On this basis, absent additional lasting damage to oil infrastructure, global oil production is projected at about 106 mb/d in 2027, returning the market to a substantial surplus in the second quarter. European natural gas prices, after surging by a projected 58 percent (y/y) this year to $19 per million British thermal units ($/mmbtu), are expected to fall by only 8 percent next year to $17.5/mmbtu—a large upward revision from the April forecast. In contrast, the U.S. benchmark is projected to remain unchanged in 2026 (y/y), and to increase by about 6 percent in 2027 and about 5 percent in 2028, mainly driven by growing external demand for LNG. Demand is expected to decrease by about 8 percent (50 bcm) in the Middle East, reflecting disrupted industrial demand. In Europe and Asia Pacific, consumption is set to soften by 2.5 percent (13 bcm) and about 1 percent (9 bcm), respectively, as power-sector use declines. By contrast, Eurasian demand is projected to rise as residential consumption rebounds after mild weather in 2025.

query: How many very strong El Niño episodes had occurred since 1950 before the current episode?

results.text: Episodes of El Niño vary considerably in intensity (figure B1.2.A).a Since 1950, there have been 27 El Niño episodes, four of which were very strong (in 1982–83, 1991–92, 1997–98, and 2015–16), with the current episode expected to become the fifth. Over the same period, there were 3 strong, 9 moderate, and 11 weak episodes. El Niño episodes typically emerge around May or June, strengthen through the third quarter of the year, peak near year-end, and dissipate during the first half of the following year. As a result, much of the associated rainfall anomaly occurs during the second half of the year, overlapping with the growing season for several major internationally traded commodities.

Episodes vary widely in intensity, and only a minority—eight out of 26 episodes since 1950—have been classified as strong or very strong.6 Commodity prices are higher during ENSO episodes than during neutral periods (box 1). However, price sensitivity differs from volatility transmission: a large movement in a commodity’s own price does not necessarily make it a stronger source of volatility for other markets. The results indicate that the strong phase of the 2015-16 El Niño was associated with much larger increases in transmitted connectedness than the weak phase (figure SF .4.B). Soybeans recorded the largest increase in connectedness during the strong phase, followed by maize. During the weak phase, maize transmission was broadly unchanged, while the increase for soybeans was similar to that for non-food commodities.

The agency also estimates an 83 percent chance that it will become the strongest El Niño since 1950 (when comparable records begin) during October–De- cember 2026 (figure 13.A).2 El Niño typically brings drier conditions to parts of Australia, Central America, the Sahel, South and Southeast Asia, and Southern Africa, and wetter conditions to parts of Central Asia, China, and the southern United States. Its effects on East Africa vary by location and season. Historically, the prices of food and beverage commodities have increased materially during El Niño episodes, as extreme weather conditions hinder production (figure 13.B). In the current episode, notable effects are expected in cocoa, palm oil, rice, and sugar markets, although annual average prices are forecast to increase significantly only for palm oil and rice.

query: In the fertilizers section, what was the average urea price in 2026Q3?

results.text: FERTILIZERSCOMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 39 Recent developments Nitrogen (urea) prices averaged $399/mt in 2026Q3, down 42 percent (q/q) and 18 percent (y/y), after peaking at $857/mt in April (figure 18.A). Prices eased further in the first half of October. The initial retreat during 2026Q2 reflected China’s easing of export restrictions in May, the temporary reduction in hostilities following the June memorandum of understand- ing between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran, and reductions in purchases, partly owing to the end of spring planting in the Northern Hemisphere. Increased exports from China and other major suppliers, including Egypt, Nigeria, and Oman, helped sustain a return to more normal price levels. China’s urea exports are expected to reach 7.0 million metric tons (mmt) in 2026, up from 4.9 mmt in 2025.

Urea prices are forecast to fall by 16 percent in 2027 and 14 percent in 2028, assuming Middle Eastern exports recover, natural gas prices ease, Fertilizers The World Bank Group’s fertilizer price index fell by 22 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q) and continued to decline in October, fully reversing the 2026Q2 surge that followed the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Urea prices drove both swings, while other fertilizer prices rose less sharply but remained elevated in 2026Q3. Despite the recent retreat, the index is projected to rise by about 14 percent in 2026 (y/y), reflecting shipping disruptions in the Middle East, associated increases in input costs, and trade restrictions. Prices are forecast to fall by 12 percent in 2027 and a further 8 percent in 2028 as input costs ease and supplies recover, aided by increased exports from producers outside the Gulf region.

MOP has been largely shielded from the Middle East conflict, as production in the Gulf region is negligible, and as potash is mined rather than produced from natural gas. Supply has also been supported by the easing of U.S. sanctions on Belarus, the third-largest producer after Canada and Russia. As a result, MOP remains the most affordable fertilizer relative to food prices (figure 18.D). Outlook and risks Despite recent declines, urea prices are projected to average 21 percent higher in 2026 (y/y), reflecting the surge in the first half of the year. Seasonal buying from Brazil, which typically purchases most of its urea imports between August and December, is likely to support prices in late 2026.

Rapidly growing investment in power grids, electric vehicle (EV) production, renewable energy, electronics, and data centers continued to support demand for aluminum, copper, and tin. Meanwhile, the ongoing slump in construction and steel activity—particularly in China—weighed on iron ore prices.

Global consumption remained broadly resilient in 2026H1, with stronger demand in China offsetting weakness elsewhere, and is expected to expand steadily, supported by investment in data centers, electrification, transport and packaging. Aluminum prices are estimated to average an all-time high of $3,250 per metric ton in 2026, about 24 percent (y/y) higher than in 2025, before easing by 5 percent in FIGURE 19 Metals and minerals markets Base metal prices remained close to all-time highs in 2026Q3, although iron ore prices weakened further amid subdued steel demand. Copper prices rose anew amid mine disruptions and increased stockpiling related to uncertainty about U.S. import tariffs. Aluminum prices have moderated after supply concerns linked to Middle East trade disruptions pushed them to record highs earlier this year, but they remain historically elevated.

Demand growth is expected to strengthen somewhat in 2027–28, supported by electronics and semiconductor applications. Solder accounts for about half of global tin use, while use in solar and other electrification technologies is growing. Following an expected 50 percent (y/y) increase in 2026 to a record annual average, tin prices are forecast to decline by 12 percent in both 2027 and 2028 as improving supply conditions ease market tightness. Zinc prices increased by 11 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q) and were little changed in October, as temporary disruptions to Chinese smelter output added to tight availability elsewhere. Mine output is expected to increase over 2027–28 as recently expanded operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo and South Africa ramp up and new capacity elsewhere in Africa comes online.

query: How many internationally traded commodities and groups does the Special Focus examine?

results.text: Most commodity analysis appropriately focuses on the supply and demand fundamentals of individual markets. While that approach remains important, it provides only a partial view when volatility associated with one commodity is linked to developments in other commodity markets. This Special Focus examines price volatility connectedness across 15 internationally traded commodities in six groups—energy, food, industrial metals, livestock, precious metals, and soft commodities (such as coffee and cotton)— using daily data from 2006 to 2026. Price volatility connectedness measures how much of the variance in a commodity’s price volatility can be explained by shocks affecting prices in other commodity markets.

SPECIAL FOCUS COMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 50 • Within-group connectedness describes the average volatility transmitted and received across commodities within a specific commodity group. Full-sample estimates characterize the underlying structure of the commodity market, while rolling estimates show how connectedness changes over time and during major episodes of global stress. FIGURE SF.1 Commodity price connectedness across markets and groups Commodity price connectedness shows no clear sustained upward or downward trend over the past two decades. Self-connectedness indexes indicate that at least three-quarters of each group’s price volatility is associated with shocks affecting that group.

SPECIAL FOCUS COMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 48 Introduction Commodity prices often move in tandem because many markets are exposed to common shifts in global activity, input costs, trade, and financial conditions. For instance, a slowdown in industrial activity can weaken demand for energy and industrial metals at the same time, while disruptions to energy supply can raise transport and fertilizer costs and spill into agricultural markets. Periods of financial or geopolitical stress can broaden these movements across otherwise distinct commodity groups (World Bank 2024). Understanding these linkages is key because commodity price shocks affect inflation, fiscal revenues, trade balances, and food and energy security, particularly in emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs) with large commodity exposures (Balcilar, Usman and Agan 2024; World Bank 2026a).
